outline.chapter_title: Why Reinforcement Learning for LLMs Needs Stability at Scale
outline.description: Motivates sequence-level reinforcement learning for large language models and frames the core stability problem GSPO solves. Introduces the setting, goals, and the observed failure modes with existing methods when scaling model size, response length, and compute.
subtopics: How large-scale RL enables deeper, longer reasoning in LLMs
Training at scale: large batches, minibatching, and off-policy effects
Catastrophic collapse with state-of-the-art methods (symptoms and why it matters)
Design desiderata for scalable RL with LLMs: stability, efficiency, simplicity

outline.description: Establishes the core notation and basic tools used throughout, including sequence likelihoods, rewards, and importance sampling.
subtopics: Policies as autoregressive language models: pi_theta(y|x) and tokenization
Sequence likelihood as product of token probabilities; log-likelihood and length
Reward models/verifiers and bounded rewards in [0,1]
On-policy vs off-policy estimation
Importance sampling principle: correcting distribution mismatch
Why clipping exists in practice (controlling off-policy drift)

outline.chapter_title: From PPO to GRPO: Value-Free RL for Language Models
outline.description: Recaps PPO and introduces GRPO as a value-free alternative that uses group-relative advantages, clarifying benefits and early appeal.
subtopics: PPO objective with token-level importance ratios and value-function advantages
Practical limitations of PPO for LLMs: value model cost and reliability on long sequences
GRPO objective: group-based advantages from multiple responses per query
How GRPO removes the value model via within-group normalization
Operational details: group size, advantage standardization, token-level clipping in GRPO

outline.chapter_title: Diagnosing Instability: The Misapplication of Token-Level Importance Weights
outline.description: Explains why GRPO becomes unstable, especially for long responses and large MoE models, by analyzing the mismatch between reward granularity and optimization unit, and the variance implications.
subtopics: Importance sampling requires averaging over many samples per distribution
GRPO’s token-level ratios use a single token sample per step ⇒ high-variance weights
Variance accumulation over long sequences; clipping amplification effects
Unit-of-reward vs unit-of-optimization mismatch: sequence-level reward vs token-level weights
Irreversibility of collapse and why tuning clipping often fails

outline.description: Introduces GSPO’s core idea: define importance ratios at the sequence level and align clipping, rewards, and optimization with the sequence unit.
subtopics: Sequence-level importance ratio s_i as geometric mean of likelihood ratios
Sequence-level clipping: accepting or rejecting entire responses for gradient use
Group-based advantage: within-query standardization for responses
Length normalization of the ratio to control variance and unify clipping scales
Why GSPO’s clipping ranges differ in magnitude from token-based methods
Alignment principle: same granularity for reward, ratio, and optimization

outline.description: Derives and interprets the gradients of GSPO and GRPO, highlighting how GSPO equalizes token weights within a response and why this reduces instability.
subtopics: GSPO gradient structure: sequence-level ratio times average token log-prob gradients
Equal token weighting within a response under GSPO
GRPO gradient structure: per-token ratios multiply per-token log-prob gradients
Impact of unequal token weights on variance and training dynamics
Long-sequence behavior: why GSPO is more robust to length and minibatching

outline.chapter_title: GSPO-token: A Flexible Variant for Token-wise Advantages
outline.description: Presents a token-level variant that preserves GSPO’s sequence-level importance weighting but allows per-token advantage shaping, useful in multi-turn or structured tasks.
subtopics: Motivation: finer-grained credit assignment without reintroducing token-level ratios
Construction of s_{i,t} using stop-gradient (detach) to keep sequence-level weighting
Numerical equivalence to GSPO when all token advantages are equal
When to prefer GSPO-token (e.g., multi-turn RL, partial credit signals)
Implementation details: detach semantics and stable optimization

outline.chapter_title: Implementing GSPO: Training Recipe and Practical Tips
outline.description: Provides a step-by-step guide to implement GSPO in LLM training pipelines, with attention to efficiency, numerical stability, and hyperparameter choices.
subtopics: End-to-end training loop with grouped responses per query
Computing sequence likelihoods efficiently (log-space accumulation, masking, padding)
Handling variable response lengths and length normalization
Reward normalization within groups and robust standardization
Choosing and tuning clipping ranges for sequence-level ratios
Interplay with KL regularization and entropy bonuses
Batching and minibatching: off-policy considerations and logging drift metrics
Monitoring: ratio distributions, clipping fractions (response-level), reward stats
Debugging instability: signs, diagnostics, and corrective actions

outline.chapter_title: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE): Stability Challenges and GSPO’s Advantage
outline.description: Explains why MoE routing volatility destabilizes GRPO and how GSPO removes the need for complex workarounds like Routing Replay.
subtopics: MoE routing: expert activation patterns and volatility across updates
Why token-level ratios become erratic under routing changes
Routing Replay: how it stabilizes GRPO and at what system cost
GSPO’s insensitivity to token-level fluctuations via sequence-likelihood focus
Practical gains: no routing cache, lower overhead, full-capacity utilization

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Evaluation: Setup, Benchmarks, and Outcomes
outline.description: Summarizes the experimental setup and key results demonstrating GSPO’s stability, efficiency, and performance versus GRPO.
subtopics: Models and training compute (e.g., Qwen3-30B-based cold-start)
Batch partitioning into minibatches and off-policy implications
Benchmarks: AIME’24, LiveCodeBench, CodeForces (metrics: Pass@1, Elo)
Clipping ranges used in practice: GSPO vs GRPO (order-of-magnitude differences)
Findings: stable reward curves, continuous gains with more compute/longer generations
Sample efficiency: better accuracy and benchmark scores at equal compute
Deployment outcome: contribution to Qwen3 model improvements

outline.description: Interprets the empirical observation that GSPO clips a much larger fraction of tokens yet trains more efficiently than GRPO.
subtopics: Observed two-orders-of-magnitude difference in clipped-token fractions
Why more aggressive sequence-level clipping can still improve efficiency
GRPO’s token-level gradients as inherently noisy signals
Design implication: quality of learning signal over quantity of tokens used

outline.chapter_title: Simplifying RL Infrastructure with Sequence-Level Likelihoods
outline.description: Discusses how GSPO’s reliance on sequence-level likelihoods reduces recomputation and precision sensitivity, offering practical engineering benefits.
subtopics: Precision mismatches between training and inference engines
Using inference-engine likelihoods directly for GSPO
Benefits in partial rollout, multi-turn RL, and disaggregated train-infer systems
Operational simplifications: fewer recomputations, reduced latency and cost

outline.description: Critically examines GSPO’s scope, potential limitations, and promising research avenues beyond the current work.
subtopics: Sensitivity to reward quality and group size
Extremely long outputs and ratio distribution tails
Interaction with auxiliary losses (e.g., KL), curriculum, and dataset refresh
Extensions to other modalities and structured generation
Connections to off-policy evaluation and per-decision importance sampling
Ablations and reproducibility considerations
Open questions: theory of variance reduction at sequence level, adaptive clipping

outline.description: Condenses the textbook into actionable guidance for applying GSPO in practice and deciding between GSPO and GSPO-token.
subtopics: Key takeaways: align unit of reward, ratio, and clipping at sequence level
When to use GSPO vs GSPO-token
Default starting hyperparameters and logging targets
Stability checklist for dense and MoE models
Troubleshooting guide and common pitfalls
